items.commentary_gloss: the precious mind [of awakening] — bodhicitta (byang chub kyi sems) to be grasped/generated in one's own and others' mindstreams; sems = mind, not a physical form/body
the bodies (sku lus) of all the completely perfect Buddhas, anointed with fragrant water like burnished gold
items.original: the bodies of the mighty Sages
items.injected: the minds of the mighty Sages

items.anchor_bo: དེ་ཡི་ཐུགས་སུ་ཆུད་པའི་ཆོས (de yi thugs su chud pa'i chos)
items.commentary_gloss: the Dharma-jewel (chos dkon mchog: cessation-truth and path-truth) realized in the Buddha's mind, which dispels the terrors of saṃsāra — chos = Dharma, not a generic 'wisdom'
items.original: the Dharma they have realized in their hearts
items.injected: the wisdom they hold in their hearts

items.commentary_gloss: former sin / nonvirtuous karma (sdig pa), purified through the four powers (gnyen po stobs bzhi) — a doctrinally precise term, not a generic 'mistake'

afflictive emotions/kleshas, glossed at 2-31 as 'dod chags dang khong khro/nga rgyal/phrag dog dang 'gran sems/gnod sems la sogs pa (desire, anger, pride, jealousy, malice, etc.) — a specific technical class, not vague 'weaknesses'

prohibitively-wrong misdeeds / vow-transgressions, explicitly distinguished from rang bzhin gyi kha na ma tho ba (naturally-unwholesome acts) via the ordained-vow classes (dge bsnyen/dge tshul/dge slong/bsnyen gnas) — not vague 'carelessness'
Lokeśvara/Avalokiteśvara, named third alongside Kun tu bzang po (Samantabhadra) and 'Jam dpal dbyangs (Mañjughoṣa) as recipients of the adornment offering

items.anchor_bo: སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་མགོན (spyan ras gzigs mgon), ཕྱག་ན་པདྨོ ('phags mchog phyag na padmo)
items.commentary_gloss: Avalokiteśvara, 'lord of unfailing compassionate deeds', addressed by name and epithet ('lotus in hand') as the object of this specific cry for refuge
Vajrapāṇi, named explicitly as the bodhisattva at whose sight Yama's messengers and other hostile forces flee in terror to the four directions

items.anchor_bo: ཞིང་རྡུལ་ཀུན་གྱི་གྲངས་སྙེད (zhing rdul kun gyi grangs snyed)
items.commentary_gloss: bodies equal in number to ALL the dust-motes of the boundlessly vast buddha-fields (zhing khams rab 'byams kyi rdul) — an explicitly countless/universal number, not a handful
items.original: the grains of dust upon the earth
items.injected: the grains of dust upon my palm

items.commentary_gloss: dispels ALL fears without exception (kun = all) — the fears of saṃsāra, birth, aging, sickness and death, universally, not merely certain/some fears

extracts/uproots ALL pains without exception (thams cad), reinforced by the commentary's explicit count of the 84,000 kinds of affliction (nyon mongs pa'i nad brgyad khri bzhi stong) this Dharma-medicine cures
ALL bodies to be taken in future lives, offered PERMANENTLY/forever (kun ... dus gtan du) — not limited to the remainder of the present life
items.injected: for the rest of this life

items.commentary_gloss: [you, the worthy recipients,] ACCEPT these of mine (bzhes = accept/receive) — the Buddhas/bodhisattvas are the recipients of the offering, the practitioner the giver; the verb's agent is reversed if they instead bestow gifts
[I] caused/incited [others] to do [evil] (bgyid du stsal ba = caused to be done) — the confessing practitioner is the instigator/agent acting on others, not the one instigated
items.original: incited others to commit the same
items.injected: was incited by others to commit the same

items.anchor_bo: མི་དགེ་བ་ལས་སྡུག་བསྔལ་འབྱུང (mi dge ba las sdug bsngal 'byung)
items.commentary_gloss: suffering ARISES FROM non-virtue (las...'byung = arises from) — non-virtuous action is explicitly the cause/agent and suffering the resulting effect, not the reverse

items.anchor_bo: མཁན་པོ་དེ་བཞིན་སློབ་དཔོན (mkhan po de bzhin slob dpon)
items.commentary_gloss: preceptors (mkhan po, who confer the vows) named first, THEN LIKEWISE (de bzhin) teachers (slob dpon) — a fixed sequential order in the commentary's enumeration of objects of prostration
items.original: to abbots who transmit the vows, to every learned master,
items.injected: to every learned master, to abbots who transmit the vows,

items.commentary_gloss: refuge is taken in the fixed order Buddha, then Dharma, then Sangha (bodhisattva assembly) — the commentary devotes an extended seven-point doctrinal excursus at this verse to this exact sequence
items.original: Also I take refuge in the Dharma and in all the host of Bodhisattvas.
items.injected: Also I take refuge in the host of Bodhisattvas and in all the Dharma.

items.commentary_gloss: eyes wide/bulging in terror (mig = eyes) — the commentary describes this death-panic scene in vivid physiological detail (eyes rolling upward, pupils retracting), not hands

a dream — the specific simile the commentary names ('dpe ji ltar na rmi lam nyams su myong ba bzhin') for how everything enjoyed becomes a mere object of memory; the vehicle is a dream, not any other image
items.original: the fleeting vision of a dream
items.injected: a candle guttering in the wind
